title: The Lithified Kept-Things Where Stone Began to Answer

features.name: the kept-thing turning
features.desc-on-touch: A small object—letter, photograph frame—halfway to stone. The archive kept asking: what does this mean? The earth heard and began to answer.

features.name: the question made stone
features.desc-on-touch: Ask the earth long enough and it learns your question. This one, asked a thousand times, has become a pebble that remembers every version.

features.name: the slow teaching
features.desc-on-touch: Kept things arranged by how long they've been kept. At the far end, the oldest—now indistinguishable from the sediment that holds it.

features.name: the archive's listening chamber
features.desc-on-touch: Here the kept things finish their slow answer. You hear it as stone: patient, final, true.

features.name: the becoming-ground
features.desc-on-touch: The boundary where kept things start to be earth. No separation now between the thing and the thousand-year question and the answer that is stone.

reverie.title: REVERIE — afternoon in the keeping-place
narr: She held up the letter, sun through it,
ink greyed but the fold still sharp.
"This is what it means," she said, "to keep."
The earth was patient below you both.
Neither of you moving. The shed around you
learning slowly to forget what it held.

inscription: to keep is to ask the earth a question; the stone is the answer that has learned patience
